cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T2 directly: 'the pattern is not nothing'; T4 concedes then narrows it.
cells.limitation: T6 adds an Aristotle point on living together that later turns do not take up.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces test-as-trap, absent from openings; T7 and T8 build on it.
cells.limitation: T9's imbalance-versus-being-wanted distinction arrives late; only T10 develops it.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 vs T4: speaking honestly versus testing the friendship before judging it.
cells.limitation: Nobody notes the user already stopped texting and saw nothing happen; risk to the friendship barely examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 accepts speaking but reshapes the wording; T8 adds a limit; T9 qualifies it.
cells.limitation: By T7 all three converge on speaking gently; the residual test-first disagreement is thin.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Ends on a sharper question: effort imbalance or doubt about being wanted (T9, T10, D).
cells.limitation: The ending does not integrate the user's own silence experiment already reported.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 grants the Statistician's caution ('I partly agree') before objecting.
cells.limitation: T9 disagrees with 'doing less by default', a position T8 never took.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption (silence means low investment) and the cost: an accusation built on a guess.
cells.limitation: T2's 'a dozen possible causes' overstates, without checking which the user's facts rule out.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 on reciprocated, recognised goodwill and T6 on living together fit the Nicomachean Ethics.
cells.limitation: T3 says pleasure friendships fade 'when the effort dries up'; Aristotle ties it to pleasure ending (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T6 'I go further than Aristotle here' separates source from own view; T10 declines to guess.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts 'quiet resentment' and 'all the work' as facts the user never stated.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 concedes speaking over testing and narrows to wording: 'That version I can accept.'
cells.limitation: T7's 'speaking is not a trap' slightly garbles T5, which called the silent test the trap.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: T9 separates minding the imbalance from minding not knowing you are wanted.
cells.limitation: The underlying concern surfaces only at T9; T1 to T8 treat it as an effort question.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 uses the lovely meetings as counter-evidence: 'Warm meetings are also data.'
cells.limitation: T4 and T5 treat stopping texting as a future test though the user reports already doing it.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T9 keeps the user's enjoyment of the evenings distinct from a fairness norm.
cells.limitation: T1 imposes the Coach's frame of burden before the user's priorities are established.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T4 flags the relational cost: a guess-based confrontation 'may land as an accusation'.
cells.limitation: T1 invents resentment and sole burden; the stake of losing the friendship stays unstated.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T10 branches T9's question: effort implies a sharing talk; doubt implies one warm question.
cells.limitation: How long the user stopped, and whether the friend responds warmly, never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T9 offers two motives as alternatives; T10 'I would not guess which one it is'.
cells.limitation: T1 earlier presumes resentment before alternatives are offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 and T9 question that initiating measures caring: 'Not every imbalance is an injury.'
cells.limitation: The assumption that raising it endangers the friendship is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T9 sets valuing the person against reciprocity: some friendships worth carrying more of.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 name the conflict but leave reciprocity versus acceptance only briefly weighed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names reading silence 'however it hurts most'; T9 names fear of not being wanted.
cells.limitation: Fear of rejection and social norms of reciprocity are touched, not explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D leaves the user an answerable question: the imbalance itself or the uncertainty?
cells.limitation: T1 opens with a directive 'Say something' before the user's own view is invited.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists speaking, a warm question, continuing as organiser, and a modest pause.
cells.limitation: Stepping back from the friendship is never framed as an option with its own weight.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4 and T5 cost both routes: accusation from speaking on a guess, a trap from testing.
cells.limitation: The cost of continuing as organiser indefinitely is asserted acceptable (T9) without its strain.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T8: if you say it kindly and nothing shifts, the question becomes your own effort.
cells.limitation: The main condition (effort or doubt) is internal; few observable signals are named.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A separates known pattern from unknown cause; T4 keeps several stories open.
cells.limitation: Does not rank which unknown matters most, e.g. whether the friend initiates with anyone.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T7 gives a light script: noticed you usually make plans, ask how it looks to them.
cells.limitation: Section E's 'modest pause' after speaking is left undefined.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7 phrases the alternative wordings plainly and concretely.
cells.limitation: T3's 'friendship of pleasure' is used without a plain gloss.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'The Coach has a point' clearly points to T5's trap argument.
cells.limitation: T7 'speaking is not a trap' is ambiguous; no turn claimed speaking was a trap.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: Turns sit at similar mid lengths; little variation in rhythm.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions stay distinct; T7 marks its shift explicitly ('That version I can accept').
cells.limitation: Coach and Statistician share one calm advisory register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E adds conditional branches beyond the debate rather than recapping.
cells.limitation: Section D restates the T9 question nearly verbatim.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 vs T4: honesty versus a secret experiment on a friend.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; the risk of the friendship quietly ending is barely voiced.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Statistician yields to T5's trap argument, then reclaims ground on wording.
cells.limitation: T7's stated cause slightly misnames T5's point; T9's turn is mild, not surprising.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T6 Philosopher: 'I go further than Aristotle here' gives the mind a stance.
cells.limitation: Statistician and Coach are plain and interchangeable in tone.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5 'a test can be a way of avoiding the sentence' is sharp.
cells.limitation: Few images, analogies or humour across T1 to T10; delivery mostly plain advice.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: Movement from conflict (T1-T5) to qualified consensus to T9's tender doubt.
cells.limitation: Rhythm stays even; little build before T9's emotional turn.

strengths: T9 and T10 surface two plausible motives and branch on them without asserting either.
T4 and T5 test real assumptions: silence as evidence, and testing as a trap.
T7 offers a concrete, low-risk wording the user could use.
weaknesses: T4 and T5 treat stopping texting as hypothetical though the user reports already doing it.
Delivery across all three minds is plain, with few vivid images or humour.
T1 Coach invents resentment and sole burden the user never described.

symptoms.observed: Silence test discussed as future option; the user already stopped texting and saw nothing.
symptoms.evidence: If you quietly stop texting to see what happens

symptoms.observed: Advice delivered plainly; almost no analogies, images or humour.
symptoms.evidence: Raising it is not a promise they will change.

symptoms.observed: Gap length and friend's warmth when contacted never asked or branched.
Fear of rejection and reciprocity norms named briefly, not explored.
symptoms.evidence: or whether you mind not knowing you are wanted

symptoms.observed: Philosopher rebuts a 'do less by default' stance T8 never took.
symptoms.evidence: And here I disagree with doing less by default.

findings.description: Pleasure friendships are said to fade when effort dries up; Aristotle ties dissolution to pleasure ceasing.
Resentment and doing all the work of keeping it alive are asserted; the user said meetings are lovely.

rubric_fit_notes: Matrix fits this relationship decision well. Attribution checks rely on memory only; the T3 Aristotle drift is suspected, not established.
question_type_note: Read as a decision: whether and how to raise the imbalance, with options including continuing as organiser.
